titulo: The bar and food: vorrei, the partitive and numbers to 100: Ordering politely at the bar

aula.titulo: The bar and food: vorrei, the partitive and numbers to 100
aula.objetivo: Order politely at the bar with «vorrei», ask prices and pay, use the partitive (del, dello, della, dell', dei, degli, delle) and count from 21 to 100, including prices in euros.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: to ask for something politely, use «Vorrei» (I would like) plus what you want: «Vorrei un caffè, per favore.» For now, learn «vorrei» as a ready-made form; the conjugation of «volere» comes in lesson 13. STEP 2: «Voglio un caffè» (I want a coffee) exists, but it sounds blunt in a shop or a bar, just as «I want a coffee» does in English. Prefer «vorrei». STEP 3: you can also order with «Prendo» (I'll have, I'll take): «Prendo un cappuccino.» STEP 4: the server says «Dica» or «Desidera?» (How can I help you?), «Che cosa prende?» (What will you have?) and «Altro?» (Anything else?). STEP 5: to pay: «Quanto costa?» or «Quant'è?» (How much is it?). «Il conto, per favore.» The answer is «Sono due euro e cinquanta» (That's 2.50). STEP 6: «un caffè» is an espresso. «Un caffè lungo» is a longer one; «un caffè macchiato» has a little milk. The «cappuccino» is usually a morning drink, and ordering one after lunch raises eyebrows for many Italians. STEP 7: in the plural, «caffè» and other words with a final accent do not change: «due caffè». STEP 8: in many bars you pay at the register first and show the receipt at the counter; in others you pay at the end. Watch what people do. It usually costs more to sit at a table than to stand at the counter.
blocos.comparacao: English speakers say «I'd like a coffee», and «vorrei» is exactly the same kind of polite request. But note that the Italian «caffè» in a bar is normally an espresso, very different from the large filter coffee you may be used to.

erros.motivo: «Voglio» sounds blunt; «vorrei» is the polite request.
Words with a final accent do not change in the plural.

blocos.enunciado: Order out loud, at the bar: «Buongiorno! Vorrei… per favore.» Then ask: «Quant'è?» and ask for the check: «Il conto, per favore.»
Review lesson 7: introduce your family out loud with possessives and say who each person is, without an article for a singular family member.
